function: Joint beam hopping (which cell each beam illuminates) and per-beam transmit power allocation in a GEO multi-beam satellite downlink (p. 1-2).
system: GEO multi-beam satellite downlink, Ka-band, phased array with 7 beams serving 30 cells, 500 MHz total bandwidth, full frequency reuse; no RIS (p. 1-3).
method: DeepMBS: parameterized deep Q-network, one agent per beam, discrete cell choice plus continuous power from a policy network, experience filtering (EFM); reinforcement learning (p. 2-4).
data_channel: Own Python simulation: downlink loss per ITU-R S.672-4 (antenna gains, free-space loss 209.6 dB, no fading model stated), DVB-S2 capacity mapping, normally distributed cell demands (p. 2-5).
test_conditions: Demand sweep 1,800 to 3,600 Mbps; Type 1 (variance 10) and Type 2 (variance 40) demand patterns; no separate training and test scenarios stated (p. 4-5).
baselines: Non-learned: Random, Greedy [9], Genetic [7]. Learned: DQN(EFM) [10] with discretized power; DeepMBS without EFM is an ablation (p. 4).
metrics: Packet loss rate, system throughput, average queuing delay, energy efficiency, normalized reward convergence (p. 4-5).
complexity: Time complexity expression of the two networks (Eqs. 16-17), simplified to O(sigma(s)+sigma(N)N(P)+sigma(N)) for a fixed structure; no runtime or FLOPs (p. 3).
openness: none; own Python simulation, no code or data link (p. 3).
q1_support: p. 2: "According to ITU-R S.672-4 [10], the downlink loss matrix" and "According to the DVB-S2 standard, the channel capacity can be expressed as"; not 3GPP TR 38.811, fixed free-space loss, no fading model. Borderline, see notes.
q2_support: p. 4: "In order to assess the generalization ability of DeepMBS (EFM), we" test Type 2 demand; p. 5: "Plan C and Plan D are compared to illustrate the" generalization, but no statement that a model trained on Type 1 is tested on Type 2 without retraining.
q3_support: p. 4: "DQN(EFM) [10]: This approach uses Deep Q-Network with" and "Random Algorithm: This approach randomly determines the illuminated cells and transmit power"; Greedy [9], Genetic [7] too; p. 1: "Du et al. [10] developed a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) based strategy combining" power and beam hopping; Fig. 2 compares throughput and energy efficiency.
q4_support: p. 3: "This section discusses the time complexity of the DeepMBS(EFM)," and "time complexity can be simplified as follows" for a fixed network structure.
q5_support: p. 3: "We implemented a Ka-band MBS system using Python for simulation experiments"; own simulator, no code or data link, no public dataset.
notes: Included, area 6: parameterized DQN jointly learns beam hopping and per-beam power in a GEO multi-beam satellite; learned beam and power control of a satellite link is physical layer. q1 is borderline for the reviewer: the paper cites ITU-R S.672-4 (an antenna-pattern standard) for the downlink loss and DVB-S2 for capacity, with a fixed free-space loss and no fading, not 3GPP TR 38.811. q2 is 0 because the generalization claim (p. 4) rests on separately configured plans (Baseline versus Plan C, p. 5) and the paper never says a model trained on Type 1 demand is tested on Type 2. DQN(EFM) [10] is counted as the earlier learned baseline although it uses the paper's own EFM; DeepMBS without EFM is an ablation.
